_why: #29, taken over from HemaSuite feature/18-gateway-consolidation. A gate that validates the resulting STATE rather than the incoming WRITE gives the caller no signal at the only moment the caller can act. Each mutation carries its own `test` key.

mutations.name: the-write-time-check-is-removed
mutations._mechanism: Back to the original defect: the disordering write returns OK and the refusal lands on the NEXT caller, who did not cause it.

mutations.name: the-check-reads-the-found-sequence-not-the-produced-one
mutations._mechanism: Re-checking `versions` is a no-op -- `classify_order` already passed on it above. This is the defect wearing the fix's clothes: the call is present, the predicate runs, and nothing is discriminated.

mutations.name: the-new-version-is-always-spliced-at-the-front
mutations._mechanism: The position must match the PLACEMENT the write will use, or a correct ascending append is evaluated as a prepend and refused. A guard that refuses valid writes is worse than no guard.
mutations.find: post.insert(0 if placement == "prepend" else len(post), new_version)

mutations.name: the-new-version-is-always-appended
mutations._mechanism: The mirror of the above, and the reason the descending control exists: a correct prepend evaluated as an append misreads a valid descending document.
mutations.find: post.insert(0 if placement == "prepend" else len(post), new_version)
